title: IRIS RegTech Solutions Ltd - 540735 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: IRIS RegTech revenue grew over 30% YoY in both Q1 and Q2 FY27; IRIS CARBON ARR jumped 52% versus March 31, 2026.
summary.overview: Management reported that revenue grew over 30% YoY in both Q1 and Q2 FY27, with commentary given on a six-month basis. Enterprise SaaS (IRIS CARBON disclosure management) was the main driver, with ARR up 52% from March 31, 2026, helped by one large enterprise deal. SupTech order intake was softer due to Middle East uncertainty, though management expects H2 to improve. Management said it will step up SaaS sales and marketing spend, and that EBITDA margin expansion is still some way off.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue growth (Q1 and Q2 FY27, YoY)

financial_highlights.change: Up from INR115 million in Q1 FY27 (+INR43 million QoQ)
Per analyst's reading of segment disclosure
Slightly lower QoQ, per analyst calculation

financial_highlights.metric: S&M spend per $1 of net ARR (H1 FY27)
financial_highlights.change: Excludes the large enterprise deal ARR; industry typically well above $1

segments.name: RegTech (IRIS CARBON, enterprise SaaS)
segments.commentary: More than 50 clients on the DM platform; ARR up 52% from March 31, 2026. Revenue rose to INR158 million in Q2 from INR115 million in Q1. Gross margin around 20% on IRIS CARBON, per management.

segments.name: SupTech (regulator solutions)
segments.commentary: New order intake was below plan due to Middle East uncertainty, with several RFPs in play and management expecting H2 to be better. Existing customers are being upsold into risk-based supervision and licensing modules. Allocated expenses rose to INR163 million from INR132 million QoQ, driven by partner payments.

segments.name: IRIS iDEAL (BFSI automated regulatory reporting)
segments.commentary: Pitching end-to-end automated reporting for larger deal sizes. A recent implementation in India is complete, and pursuits are under way in Mauritius and Qatar. Sales cycles are long.

segments.name: Other / Unallocated
segments.commentary: Other business includes long-running RBI content and website work, which accounts for the gap between the ARR total and the sum of the product ARRs (around INR3 crore in H1 and INR5 crore in H2 FY26). Unallocated expenses are corporate costs such as management salaries and rent.

guidance_outlook: Target SaaS revenue growth of about 35% a year; management says this target was surpassed halfway through FY27 but more work remains.
Management plans a higher outlay on SaaS sales and marketing; S&M spend is to be kept at about $1.0-1.4 per $1 of net ARR.
Management said beyond the $1.0-1.4 range EBITDA margins should start expanding, but it is 'a little early' to expect meaningful expansion.
H2 expected to be stronger than H1 on revenue and profitability; higher RegTech ARR should lift revenue as Q3 unfolds.
Management aims to balance SaaS customer acquisition costs with SupTech and iDEAL profits to keep EBITDA carefully managed.
Revenue trajectory expected to trend up, but growth will not be linear, per CFO.
capex_capacity: No capacity, capex or commissioning figures were given on the call.
Product suite being widened for SupTech customers: risk-based supervision, licensing and other modules, aimed at a one-stop regulatory reporting offering.
AI features are bundled into existing products such as IRIS CARBON; not sold as a standalone offering or separate P&L.
demand_pricing: SupTech new orders delayed by Middle East uncertainty; existing customers are sending change requests and the company is still able to execute current work. Management said conditions have improved since end-Q1.

Enterprise SaaS wins come from replacement of incumbent disclosure management platforms, typically timed to contract renewal. Differentiators cited: fast onboarding, Office 365 integration, XBRL and structured reporting, and POCs.
Management is building the IRIS CARBON brand in the U.S. market and expanding partner networks.
Strong ARR increase partly reflects one large enterprise deal; management says the growth in ARR and revenue is not linear.

qa_highlights.question: How does IRIS CARBON acquire clients already using another disclosure management platform?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepta Rangarajan said the company engages early, keeps prospects warm, and pitches around contract renewal. Bala added that fast onboarding and Office 365 integration help switching. POCs and limited workshops are offered in some cases.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI agent a separate line of business with its own P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: No. AI features are bundled into products such as IRIS CARBON and offered to regulatory and enterprise customers; they are not a standalone product at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise faster than revenue, and can S&M spend be disclosed separately?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO agreed to show S&M separately going forward. Management said it has not disclosed hard S&M numbers, but will give indications; the metric given is under $1 of S&M per $1 of net ARR in H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the difference between the ARR total and the sum of product ARRs?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap relates to a long-running service for the Reserve Bank of India covering content and website management, which is reported under the other business (around INR3 crore in H1 and INR5 crore in H2 FY26).

qa_highlights.question: Why did SupTech allocated expenses rise while RegTech allocated expenses fell QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: SupTech: partner payments rose along with revenue. RegTech: a small drop, attributed to less travel during a vacation period in some markets in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q2 RegTech revenue jump (+INR43 million QoQ) continue, and when will EBITDA margins expand?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vineet Kandoi said the trajectory would be upward but not linear. The CEO said EBITDA margin depends on S&M spend; margins should expand beyond about $1.0-1.4 S&M per $1 net ARR, but expansion is still early.

risks_watch: Middle East uncertainty is delaying new SupTech orders; management said customers are guarded about new spend.
Sustained S&M spend is expected to pressure EBITDA margins in the near term; the company has not disclosed separate S&M figures.
Lumpy ARR: part of the 52% ARR increase came from one large enterprise deal.
SupTech H2 recovery depends on converting several RFPs; sales cycles in iDEAL are long.
Management said the sub-$1 S&M per $1 of net ARR efficiency may not persist.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and ARR momentum, but cautious on near-term margins and on SupTech order inflow, which management ties to Middle East uncertainty. Management was open about EBITDA margin expansion being 'a little early' and avoided a firm target for S&M disclosure.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report that over the past six months; we have sustained our growth momentum with revenues growing at over 30% on a Y-o-Y basis in both the first and second quarters of this financial year.
The annual recurring revenue, ARR, of IRIS CARBON jumped 52% from the number as of March 31st, 2026.
My sense is we are a little early to start meaningfully expanding the EBITDA margins, but we will get there sooner than later.
We want to keep the ratio fairly competitive at around that $1 -$1.4 sales and marketing per $1 of net ARR earned.

growth.why: Management reiterated SaaS growth of about 35% a year, saying the target was surpassed at halfway through FY27, with revenue growth over 30% YoY in both Q1 and Q2; no new capacity, capex or commissioning was given, and backing is demand-led (IRIS CARBON ARR up 52% since March 31, 2026, partly one large deal) with SupTech orders softer on Middle East uncertainty.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says S&M will rise to about $1.0-1.4 per $1 of net ARR and EBITDA margin expansion is 'a little early', with H1 S&M at a little under $1 per $1 of net ARR, which may not persist.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capacity, plant, line or commissioning figures were given on the call.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue grew over 30% YoY in both Q1 and Q2 FY27, RegTech revenue rose to INR158 million in Q2 from INR115 million in Q1, and IRIS CARBON ARR is up 52% since March 31, 2026, though partly from one large deal.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex was discussed and utilisation was not given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: The ~35% SaaS growth target was surpassed at the halfway point of FY27, but management kept the target unchanged with no new numeric guide and says growth will not be linear.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: SupTech new orders were below plan on Middle East uncertainty with several RFPs unconverted, and management expects H2 to improve on that conversion.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: SupTech product suite is being widened with risk-based supervision, licensing and other modules, but no launch dates or numbers were given.

rows.label: SupTech upsell into risk-based supervision and licensing modules
rows.why: Existing customers are sending change requests and being upsold into new modules, but no value or timing was quantified.

rows.label: SupTech H2 order recovery from RFP conversion
rows.why: Management expects H2 orders to improve as several RFPs are in play, but Middle East uncertainty is holding back customer spend.

rows.label: IRIS iDEAL pursuits in Mauritius and Qatar
rows.why: Pursuits are under way in Mauritius and Qatar after a recent India implementation, but sales cycles are long and no deal count was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on SaaS growth and ARR momentum, but cautious on near-term EBITDA margins, S&M disclosure and SupTech order inflow tied to Middle East uncertainty; the brief gives no analyst question tone, so analysts are read as probing from the Q&A topics on S&M and margins.
